dependencies on C++11 features in Stan itself, but that
someone wanted to add some C++11 features to the tests,
which at the time, seemed OK. If that's what's breaking
our builds, I think we should reverse that decision and
not depend on C++11 in the tests, either.

On Friday, December 7, 2012 6:31:34 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
The builds being broken on Jenkins is blocking the
release of a new version of Stan.  Not to mention
totally stressing me out because I have no idea how to
even begin to debug the problem.

Were the problems introduced by a new dependency
on C++11?   I remember deciding that we would have no
dependencies on C++11 features in Stan itself, but that
someone wanted to add some C++11 features to the tests,
which at the time, seemed OK.  If that's what's breaking
our builds, I think we should reverse that decision and
not depend on C++11 in the tests, either.

I think there are two separate issues here: One is whether the tests should utilize features that are unique to the C++11 standard, which I guess Daniel has good reason to want. The other is whether Stan itself should adhere to the C++11 standard even if we are not using any of its unique features like decltype or lambda functions or whatever.

I think the problems we are having are related to the second issue, but it is a good goal to target the standard. If -std is unspecified, it defaults to g++99, which is not an actual standard. The reason why I think we are utilizing some quirky undefined behavior is that we are having more success with the old compilers. As far as I know, all versions of (pure) g++ up to 4.6.x are passing test-unit. It is g++-4.7 and clang-3.1 and the forthcoming release of each that are having trouble, plus mingw on Windows. That mingw is close to g++-4.6, but I can successfully cross-compile to Windows, so I think we would be okay if Jenkins weren't mysteriously dying.

I can't even get compiled with clang++ -O0 with Ben's suggestions,
putting the following in stan/make

    CFLAGS += -std=c++0x

and removing from stan/make/os_mac

    CFLAGS_GTEST += -Wno-c++11-extensions

The compiler exits in the middle of an Eigen library:

Can you get through the Eigen test suite with those options?

We should have released v1.0.4 as soon as the thing with the line numbers in the error message was fixed. And we shouldn't have tried to transition to the c++11 standard in a branch rather than in master. But I think we should keep trying to move forward rather than trying to go backward.

Ben

It is hard to say that going backwards is the right direction without knowing what the problem is. That said, if we do

CFLAGS_GTEST += -std=c++0x

rather than

CFLAGS += -std=c++0x

(which I think was Daniel's original intention), then we still have test failures in src/test/gm/parser_test.cpp (for recent compilers only). However, these test failures are not that bad: stanc is parsing the .stan files fine, but parser_test.cpp does not utilize stanc. In other words, something in these headers

#include "stan/gm/ast_def.cpp"
#include "stan/gm/parser.hpp"
#include <stan/gm/generator.hpp>
#include <stan/gm/grammars/program_grammar_def.hpp>
#include <stan/gm/grammars/whitespace_grammar_def.hpp>
#include <stan/gm/grammars/expression_grammar_def.hpp>
#include <stan/gm/grammars/statement_grammar_def.hpp>
#include <stan/gm/grammars/var_decls_grammar_def.hpp>

is likely to be not compliant with the c++11 standard (i.e. we are getting the same error from both g++ >= 4.7 and clang++ >= 3.1 and with either boost 1.52 or 1.50). But no one actually parses without stanc, and it's a non-issue with the default versions of g++ on Mac and Windows anyway. So, I don't think it would be the worst thing in the world to blacklist that test, release v1.0.4, and then try to make all of Stan standard compliant for v1.0.5.
